name: Beelzebub
overview: The Scriptures reveal Beelzebub as the prince or chief of devils, a title used by Jesus' opponents to accuse Him of casting out demons by demonic power (Matthew 12:24; Mark 3:22; Luke 11:15). Jesus confronts this charge by illustrating the absurdity of Satan working against himself and challenges the logic behind attributing His authority to Beelzebub (Luke 11:18; Matthew 12:27). Additionally, the name Beelzebub appears in the context of messengers sent by Ahaziah, indicating its recognition in broader biblical narratives. These passages emphasize the spiritual conflict surrounding Christ’s ministry and affirm His divine authority over demonic forces.
